subject: relationships
topic: The more compatible you are, the less satisfied you feel over time
angle: While satisfaction can lead to a perception of similarity, actual personality similarity is unrelated to relationship satisfaction in some studies and positively associated with satisfaction in others.
title: The Myth of Compatibility

hooks.text: Do you need to be similar to be happy?
You assume similarity breeds love. The evidence is mixed.
You are mistaking your own happiness for shared traits.
Two people, different traits, one shared room.
Similarity is not a universal predictor of satisfaction.

reveal.headline: Similarity is not a universal predictor of satisfaction.
reveal.body: Some studies show personality similarity is unrelated to satisfaction, while others find it is positively associated.

explain.headline: Satisfaction may create the perception of similarity.
explain.body: Research shows that people who are more satisfied with their friendships perceive those friends as more similar to themselves. The evidence is mixed and depends on what type of similarity is measured.

matters.headline: You might be looking for the wrong signal.
matters.body: That may be why you feel a connection even when your personalities differ. You might be perceiving common ground because you enjoy the bond, not because it exists.

example.headline: A quiet dinner at a kitchen table.
example.body: You sit across from someone who thinks differently than you do. You laugh at a joke and feel a sense of closeness in the shared space of the room.

question.headline: Is the bond real, or just a reflection of your own happiness?

verdict: The evidence is inconsistent, showing that similarity is not a universal predictor of satisfaction and may instead be a byproduct of satisfaction.
caveat: The findings vary significantly depending on whether the study measures actual similarity, perceived similarity, or specific types of similarity like political attitudes.
caption:
Compatibility is not a straight line.

Research shows that similarity is not a universal predictor of relationship satisfaction. While some studies find a link between actual similarity and satisfaction, others find no connection at all. The results vary depending on whether the study measures perceived similarity or specific types like political attitudes.
